business_problem: Grupo Falabella needed to turn AI into a cross-functional business capability that improves customer experience, sales conversion, service responsiveness, and logistics efficiency across its five business units rather than leaving AI confined to technical teams.
solution_summary: Grupo Falabella is implementing a portfolio of in-house AI services across ecommerce, banking, customer service, and logistics rather than a single isolated model. Browsing and purchasing patterns from the group’s websites and mobile applications are processed by hyper-personalization and semantic algorithms to decide which products, benefits, and recommendations each user sees. Those recommendations are surfaced in the Banco Falabella app and can redirect demand into Falabella.com, where the company attributes US$78 million in sales to the system over 12 months. At Sodimac, a virtual assistant uses customer prompts to assemble project material lists and link them to purchasable items. Falabella also uses generative AI to automate frequent customer-service questions with human handoff, while cameras plus computer vision estimate truck cargo volume in real time for dispatch planning. The article names a shared technology backbone connecting retail, banking, payments, shopping centers, and digital channels, but does not specify the storage platforms behind it.

data_flow: Browsing and purchasing patterns from Falabella websites and mobile apps feed hyper-personalized recommendation logic, which is served in channels such as the Banco Falabella app and can redirect customers to Falabella.com. In Sodimac, customer project descriptions are processed by a virtual assistant that returns material lists linked to products. In logistics, cameras capture truck images and computer vision estimates load volume in real time for dispatch decisions.
